claims.text: Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The initial inter-lamellar spacing is approximately 2 μm.
The initial alloy has a fracture stress of approximately 944 MPa.
The initial alloy has an elongation of approximately 25.6%.
The initial alloy's ductility is limited by stress concentration at incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Applying 6 GPa at 1473 K for 2 hours in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus will topologically transform the lamellae.
The HPHT-induced topology will be a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
HPHT treatment will replace incoherent lamellar boundaries with coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces will facilitate dislocation transfer between the two phases.
The transformed microstructure will promote stacking-fault formation.
The transformed microstructure will promote deformation twinning.
The enabled deformation mechanisms will produce a more homogeneous strain distribution.
Homogeneous strain distribution and dislocation transfer will reduce interfacial stress concentration and arrest interfacial cracking.
HPHT treatment will significantly improve ductility without sacrificing strength.
The treated alloy will exhibit elongated cracks, whereas the baseline exhibits isolated microcracks.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
The as-cast baseline has divergent GND densities between its phases.
The FCC/B2 structure has a pressure-temperature stability window beyond which phase decomposition or loss of eutectic structure occurs.
Conventional thermomechanical treatments fail to produce the same hierarchical interface coherence or GND homogenization.

contradictions.description: The task describes the initial alloy as homogenized, whereas the hypothesis defines the comparison baseline as as-cast; it does not clarify whether the homogenized and as-cast states are intended to be identical.
